title: Geelen's coarse Gallai conjecture for A-paths
statement: Let $G$ be a finite or infinite graph and let $A\subseteq V(G)$. An **$A$-path** is a path in $G$ between two distinct vertices of $A$. Two subgraphs are at distance at least $r$ when the distance between their vertex sets is at least $r$. A set is **$(a,b)$-centered** if it is contained in the union of at most $a$ balls of radius at most $b$. **Geelen's coarse Gallai conjecture.** There exist functions $f,g:\mathbb N\rightarrow\mathbb R$ such that for any $k,r\in\mathbb N$, graph $G$ and $A\subseteq V(G)$, either there exist $k$ $A$-paths pairwise at distance in $G$ at least $r$, or there exists a set $(f(k),g(r))$-centered in $G$ intersecting all $A$-paths. The conjecture is a coarse version of Gallai's packing-covering theorem for $A$-paths. The source does not state a resolution; its exact original formulation was reported as lost, and this is the formulation attributed to Geelen by Hendrey and Jacobs.
source_name: Chun-Hung Liu, “Coarse Menger property of quasi-minor excluded graphs and length spaces”, arXiv:2605.10068 (2026).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2512.17232](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17232).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10068

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2026). “Their counterexamples also disprove the cases for any pair $(k,r)$ with $k \geq 3$ and $r \geq 3$ and imply that Conjecture remains false even if the bound $cr$ for the radius of balls is changed to any function of $k$ and $r$.”
